**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 61, verses 1–14**

It is a Meccan surah. It contains nine hundred letters, two hundred and twenty-one words, and fourteen verses.

We were told by Abu al-Hasan al-Hayazi, who said: Ibn Habash related to us, who said: Abu Abbas Muhammad ibn Musa al-Razi related to me, who said: Abdullah ibn Rawh al-Mada'ini related to us, who said: Shababa ibn Sawwar al-Ghazari related to me, who said: Makhlad ibn Abd al-Wahid related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd and from Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Ibn Habash, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Isa (peace be upon him), Isa will be praying for him and asking forgiveness for him for as long as he is in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be his companion." [283] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/459.]]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

*"Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do? God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as if they were a solid structure."*

Muqatil said: Before they were commanded to fight, the believers said: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, the Exalted, we would do them and spend our wealth and our lives on them." So God guided them to the deed most beloved to Him, saying: *"God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as if they were a solid structure."* He explained this to them, and then on the Day of Uhud they were tested by it, and they turned their backs on the Prophet (ﷺ) in flight. So God, the Exalted, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi said: The believers said: "O Messenger of God, if we knew the most beloved deeds, we would do them." Then there was revealed: *"Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?"* The speech then broke off, and he did not explain anything to them. They remained as long as God willed, saying: "If only we knew what it is! By God, if we did, we would buy it with our wealth, our lives, and our families." So God guided them, saying: *"Believe in God and His Messenger, and strive in the cause of God..."* (the verse). They were tested by this on the Day of Uhud, when they fled from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) after he was struck down, his face was wounded, and his lower front tooth was broken. So this verse was revealed rebuking them for failing to keep their word.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: When God, the Exalted, informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of the reward of the martyrs of Badr, the Companions said: "If we meet a battle after this, we will exert ourselves fully in it." Then they fled on the Day of Uhud, so God rebuked them with this verse.

Ibn Abbas said: Some of the believers, before jihad was enjoined, were saying: "We wish that God would show us the deed most beloved to Him, so that we might do it." So God, the Exalted, informed them that the best deed is faith without any doubt, and jihad. Some of them disliked this, and jihad was difficult for them, so they held back from it. Then God, the Exalted, revealed this verse.

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: These two verses were revealed concerning fighting. A man would say, "I have killed," when he had not fought; "I have stabbed," when he had not stabbed; "I have struck," when he had not struck; "I have endured," when he had not endured.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Muqallab related to us, who said: Abu al-Harith Ahmad ibn Sa'id related to us in Damascus, who said: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri related to us, who said: Husayn ibn Hudhayf al-Suhri informed us, who said:

My paternal uncle related to me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Suhayb, who said: There was a man on the day of Badr who had harmed the Muslims and opposed them. Suhayb killed him in the battle. A man said, "O Messenger of God, Suhayb has killed so-and-so." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was pleased with that. Then Amr ibn Abd al-Rahman said to Suhayb: "Inform the Prophet (ﷺ) that you killed him, for so-and-so is claiming it." Suhayb said: "I killed him only for God and His Messenger." Amr ibn Abd al-Rahman said: "O Messenger of God, Suhayb killed him." He said: "Is that so, O Abu Yahya?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." Then God, the Exalted, revealed: *"O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?"* and the other verse.

Al-Hasan said: These were the hypocrites. God called them and attributed to them the declaration they had proclaimed to the Muslims. So God revealed: *"O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?"*, that is, falsely and deceitfully.

Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites who promised the believers victory while they were liars.

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning a group of the Ansar, among them Abdullah ibn Rawaha, who said in one of their gatherings: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, we would do them until we die." So God, the Exalted, revealed this surah. Abdullah ibn Rawaha then said: "I will not cease to be a man confined in the way of God until I die or am killed." He was killed as a martyr at Mu'tah. May God have mercy on him and be pleased with him.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: It was revealed concerning the man who praises himself for what his peers have not done, and who loves to be praised for what he has not done.

Abu al-Qasim al-Husayni related to us, in wording, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus al-Tara'ifi related to us, who said: My paternal uncle Sa'id al-Darimi related to us, who said: Mahbub ibn Musa al-Antaki related to us, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: We went out discussing, and we said: "Which of us will ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ) which deeds are most beloved to God?" Then we dispersed, each of us wishing that one of us would go to him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent for us and gathered us, and he began to point from one of us to another, and he recited to us *"Whatever is in the heavens..."* until the end.

Abu Salama said: Abdullah ibn Salam recited it to us until the end. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said: Abu Salama recited it to us until the end. Al-Awza'i said: Yahya ibn Ishaq recited it to us until the end. Abu Ishaq al-Fazari said: Al-Awza'i recited it to us until the end. Mahbub ibn Musa said: Al-Fazari recited it to us until the end. Uthman ibn Sa'id said: Mahbub recited it to us until the end. Al-Tara'ifi said: Uthman ibn Sa'id recited it to us until the end. Al-Qasim said: Abu al-Hasan al-Tara'ifi recited it to us until its end, and al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim recited it to us until the end, and we asked Ahmad al-Tha'labi to recite, and he recited to us until the end.

***Kabura maqtan*** (*kabura* here is a verb of wonder, and *maqtan* is in the accusative): it is in the accusative as a state (*hal*, a circumstantial accusative), and it may also be read as a specification (*tamyiz*, an accusative clarifying what is meant).

Al-Kisa'i said: *An taqulu* is in the nominative position, because *kabura* functions like your saying *bi'sa rajulan akhuka* ("how bad a man your brother is"). The reciters supplied a hidden nominative subject in it. *Al-maqt* and *al-maqata* are one and the same verbal noun. One says *rajul mamqut* and *muqayyat* when people do not love him.

*"God loves those who fight in His cause"* who do not turn away from their positions, *"in ranks, as if they were a solid structure"*, which is firmly joined together, meaning fixed, secure, and without any gap or flaw. Its root is from *al-rasas* (lead), and from it comes the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Close up your ranks in the rows, lest the devils fill the gaps between you, as if they were young goats." [284] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 5/387, with variation.]]

*"And when Musa said to his people, from the Children of Israel: O my people, why do you harm me, when you know that I am the Messenger of God to you?"* This was when they threw at him the accusation of defect. The Messenger is to be honored and respected. *"So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate from the truth"*, from the religion. *"And God does not guide the defiant people."* 

*"And when Isa son of Maryam said: O Children of Israel, I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and giving good news of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad."* He is the one who is not to be blamed. There are two views on its meaning. The first is that all the prophets praise God, and our Prophet (ﷺ) is Ahmad, that is, he praises God more than they do. The second is that all the prophets are praised, and our Prophet is Ahmad, that is, he has more virtues and gathers more excellences.

*"But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said: This is evident magic. Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God while he is being invited to Islam? And God does not guide the unjust people. They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it. He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it."*

*"O you who believe, shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment?"* The reading of the common reciters is with light stress, from *al-inja'* (to save). Ibn Amir read it with emphasis, from *al-tanjiya*, [...]. *"That you believe in God and His Messenger, and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you knew. He will forgive you your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings."*

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Harjah related to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Farah al-Baghdadi related to us, who said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad ibn Jubayr al-Qassab related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: We asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about them, and he said: "A palace of pearl in Paradise, and that palace has seventy houses of red ruby, in each house seventy chambers of green emerald, in each chamber seventy beds, on each bed seventy kinds of coverlets, on each coverlet a woman of the dark-eyed houris, in each chamber seventy tables, on each table seventy kinds of food, in each chamber seventy male and female servants." He said: "God gives the believer strength for his food alone, sufficient for all of that." [285] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/420; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/88.]]

*"In the Gardens of Eden. That is the great triumph. And another favor you love: victory from God and an imminent conquest. So give good tidings to the believers."* The grammarians of Basra said: *wa ukhra* is in the genitive position (that is, it is joined to *tijara*), meaning "and a commerce of another kind." The grammarians of Kufa said: its position is nominative, meaning "and for you there is another in this world, along with the reward of the next."

Then God urged them to support the religion and to fight its opponents, saying: *"O you who believe, be helpers of God."* That is, helpers with the sword against His enemies. Abu Amr and the people of the Hijaz read *ansaran* with tanwin, which is the choice of Ayyub. The rest read it as a construct (*idafa*), which is the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu Ubayd, because God said *"We are God's helpers"*, and did not say *ansaran li-llah*.

*"As Isa son of Maryam said to the disciples: Who are my helpers toward God? The disciples said: We are God's helpers. Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, and a group disbelieved. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant."*
